items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...you were going to talk about some of the things that you found there that you said you had forgotten you did. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, yeah. I'm looking here, The Red Callender Six...

ctx.x: Not real Jazz, no. I would say he was amazing for 17 years old, but he hadn't developed a style. He just had all the facility.

This listing came from Rust. Earlier we were looking at the listings for you in the Jepsen discography, and you were going to talk about some of the things that you found there that you said you had forgotten you did.

Oh, yeah. I'm looking here, The Red Callender Six. That was with Herbie Haymer, Arnold Ross, Les Paul, Shadow Wilson. That's when we did "These Foolish Things" and an original, "Ode To A Giant," "Get Happy" featuring Sweets Edison, "I Cover The Waterfront" which featured Sweets, and "Lady, Be Good."
